description: Translations for any .NET 10+ app, written in C# and checked at compile time: a class per language, inline texts, or an attribute on a type or its members. A missing translation, or one that never uses a value the original shows, is a build error. No resource files, no dependencies, safe to trim and to publish with Native AOT.
releaseNotes:
A text takes a value as a method of its set. Write Greeting(string name) in each language and call ShopLocalization.Greeting(customer.Name). LocalizableText.Format is gone, and nothing fills in a placeholder such as {0} any more, so a wording that holds one shows its braces (LOC502, with an IDE fix that writes the method). A text passed to a string parameter of such a method is a build warning (LOC303, with an IDE fix that makes the parameter a LocalizableText), because it keeps the wording of the language in use at the call. A text follows a culture passed as a format provider, as in string.Create(culture, ...) and string.Format(culture, ...). Each language writes its own plurals in C#, because a wording can depend on its values.

A set can hold the texts of an enum. List ILocalizationSet<OrderStatus> in place of ILocalizationSet, and every member of the enum needs a text in every language (CS0535). order.Status.GetText() gives a value its text, and so does OrderStatusLocalization.GetTextByValue(order.Status).

A label can sit on the member it names. Mark a property, a field, an enum member or a type [Localized(en: "City", nl: "Plaats")], with a wording per language. LocalizableText.GetTextByMember<Address>(nameof(Address.City)) gives the text, also by a Type or a PropertyInfo your code holds. LocalizableText.GetTextOfType<Address>() gives the text of a type itself, and a value of an enum gives the text of its member with GetText(). The source generator writes each text as code, so nothing reads the attribute at run time. The Key of such a text is the member's name, and its FullKey is the member's full name, such as Shop.Domain.Address.City. A member of an enum without [Localized] next to members that have it is a build warning (LOC503).

The build holds every language to the values. A language whose method never uses a value the default wording shows doesn't build (LOC302), and neither does a language of LocalizableText.Inline that leaves out a value the default language shows.

The names say localization. A set implements ILocalizationSet and its contract: class ShopLocalizationNl : ILocalizationSet, IShopLocalization. The registry is LocalizationRegistry, and [ExcludeFromLocalizationDiscovery] keeps a set or a member out. A set's name ends in its language in PascalCase, such as ShopLocalizationEnGb for en-GB, and an inline text takes enGb: for it. A class that lists only a contract is no set. A set states its language in LocalizationLanguageCode, which was LanguageCode: string ILocalizationSet.LocalizationLanguageCode => "en-GB". LocalizableText.GetWording(set) replaces GetTranslation(set).

ResourceText is part of LocalizableText, which has the Key, the FullKey, the Contract and the Arguments. The Key of a text of a set is its name, such as Checkout, and its FullKey is its full name, such as MyApp.Localization.ShopLocalization.Checkout. Read FullKey where you look a text up in a shared resource file. LocalizableText.Keyed(key, defaultText) replaces new ResourceText(key, defaultText).

Every generated class has a method GetTextByKey, for a key your code only has at run time. ShopLocalization.GetTextByKey("Checkout") gives the text, and GetTextByKey("Greeting", customer.Name) a text with parameters. A key no text has throws. No text can be named GetTextByKey any more (LOC205).

Two texts are equal when they show the same wording for the current UI culture, as two strings are. A text also equals a string with that wording.

LocalizationRegistry.CurrentUICultureProvider gives the user's culture in an app that keeps it somewhere other than CultureInfo.CurrentUICulture.

The codes of the build's messages are grouped by subject, from LOC100 to LOC601. The page docs/build-errors.md lists each one, and six of them have an IDE fix.

The details have a page per subject under docs/, which the README links to. New is a page on performance, with measurements next to IStringLocalizer.
